title: The more Putin escalates his attacks on Europe, the more Europe should support Ukraine – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Garton Ash argues Putin is escalating both the war in Ukraine and a shadow hybrid war on Europe to break support for Kyiv, so Europe should double down on Ukraine; he credits Germany's central role but flags fraying political support and a possible EUR 100bn funding gap in 2027.

themes.theme: Putin's dual war and the case for backing Ukraine

insights.claim: Putin is escalating both the full-scale war in Ukraine and a shadow hybrid war against Europe, primarily to break European support for Ukraine so he can subjugate it.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: European hybrid attacks (drones, sabotage, disinformation) should be read as pressure aimed at Ukraine aid, not standalone events.
insights.locator: Vladimir Putin is escalating both his full-scale war

insights.claim: Europe's central response should be to redouble support for Ukraine, because only there, not in a contest of a thousand hybrid pinpricks, can Russia be meaningfully defeated and deterred.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: Supports continued and rising European defence and Ukraine-aid spending.
insights.locator: It’s there, and only there, not in a contest of a thousand hybrid pinpricks

insights.claim: Historian Martin Schulze Wessel argues Putin's policy fits an older Russian tradition of territorial expansionism and imperial ideology, and that Russia is 'the most dangerous country in the world'; Garton Ash says it certainly is for Europe.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: Undermines the view that NATO enlargement drives Russian behaviour, implying a long-horizon European security threat.

insights.claim: Russian expansion was historically facilitated by other great powers and halted by equal opposing powers; since Trump's return the US no longer plays the opposing role, leaving Europe as the equal and opposing power.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: Europe is carrying deterrence of Russia, supporting structural growth in European defence outlays.
insights.locator: Russia’s expansion was always facilitated by cooperation with other great powers

themes.theme: Germany's central role and European capacity

insights.claim: Europe including Britain has given more aid to Ukraine than the US, its combined economies are 10 times Russia's, and Germany's is twice Russia's.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: Europe has the economic capacity to outspend Russia on this war; the constraint is political will.
insights.locator: Europe (including Britain) has now given more aid to Ukraine than the US.

insights.claim: Per the Kiel Institute tracker Germany is the biggest individual country donor to Ukraine after the US, giving twice as much as Britain or France, and has donated 19 air-defence systems including five Patriot batteries, two more than the US.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: German industry and budget are the key supply node for European air defence.
insights.locator: Cumulatively, since the beginning of the full-scale war in 2022

insights.claim: German defence spending is projected by the finance ministry to reach EUR 154bn in 2028, roughly equal to Russia's estimated total military expenditure this year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: Supports sustained demand for German and European defence contractors.

insights.claim: Chancellor Merz travelled by train to Kyiv on October 3rd with defence industry leaders, and Russian bombardment of central Kyiv continued during the visit.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: Defence-industry delegations to Kyiv suggest deepening German-Ukrainian industrial cooperation.
insights.locator: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has shown that will, and courage

insights.claim: Germany is a prime target of Russia's hybrid war, including explosive-laden drones at Leipzig airport attributed to Russia by the German government, assassination threats against defence industry bosses and covert interference.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: German defence firms and infrastructure face physical and security risk; expect higher security spending.
insights.locator: Precisely because Putin sees Germany’s centrality

themes.theme: Fraying European political support and funding gap

insights.claim: Support for Ukraine is eroding politically: AfD would abandon Ukraine, Le Pen's National Rally says France cannot afford to keep giving, two smaller Polish parties are anti-Ukrainian, and an Italian poll found over half opposed to continued weapons deliveries.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: Elections in Germany, France and elsewhere are the key risk to long-term European Ukraine aid.
insights.locator: A sceptic can point to many grounds for pessimism.

insights.claim: Experts estimate as much as EUR 100bn of additional support for Ukraine may be needed in 2027 alone, while taxpayers are unwilling and enthusiasm for using Russian frozen assets held in Belgium evaporates.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: Frozen-asset use and EU-level financing are the likely fiscal battleground for 2027.
insights.locator: experts estimate as much as €100bn of additional support

insights.claim: Putin believes decadent European democracies will crumble before an imperialist strongman's determination, and the winter ahead tests Germany's resolve, democracies' staying power and European unity.
insights.speaker: Timothy Garton Ash
insights.so_what: Winter 2026-27 is a stress test for European unity on Ukraine.
insights.locator: Putin believes decadent European democracies will crumble
